prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- “Real change” to rebalance wealth and power, tackle the climate emergency, rebuild public services, and raise living standards.

Investment, ownership and funding
- £400bn National Transformation Fund (incl. £250bn Green Transformation Fund) and a National Investment Bank plus Regional Development Banks to drive decarbonisation, jobs and productivity.
- End the “outsourcing presumption”; insource public services; take PFI contracts back over time.
- Tax changes: reverse parts of Tory corporation tax cuts; higher income tax only for earnings over £80k; no rise in VAT; major crackdown on avoidance/evasion; fairer tax on wealth.

Green Industrial Revolution
- Target: majority of emissions cuts by 2030; 1m green jobs; delist firms that don’t align with climate goals.
- Energy: 90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low-carbon by 2030; 7,000 offshore and 2,000 onshore turbines; major solar; trial tidal/hydrogen; ban fracking; upgrade nearly all 27m homes; zero‑carbon new homes; windfall tax on oil firms.
- Public ownership: bring energy networks/supply and water into democratic public hands.

Transport and environment
- Rail brought into public ownership; full electrification; complete HS2 to Scotland; “Crossrail for the North”; expand rail freight.
- Councils empowered to run buses; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils take control; restore 3,000 routes; invest in walking/cycling.
- Aim to end new petrol/diesel sales by 2030; mass EV charging rollout.
- New Clean Air Act; stronger flood defences; legally binding nature recovery targets; major tree planting; producer responsibility for waste; bottle return schemes; ban badger cull; protect animal welfare.

NHS and social care
- NHS funding up avg 4.3%/yr; end and reverse privatisation; repeal Health and Social Care Act; free prescriptions for all and free basic dentistry; invest in scanners, IT and staffing; mental health parity with 24/7 crisis services; modernise facilities.
- National Care Service: free personal care (starting with older people), cap lifetime costs, end 15‑minute visits, better pay/conditions for care workers.

Work, rights and pay
- Real Living Wage of at least £10 for all 16+; ban zero‑hours; rights from day one; sectoral collective bargaining; strengthen unions; tackle late payments; move toward 32‑hour average week within a decade with no loss of pay.
- Inclusive Ownership Funds (up to 10% of large firms) to share dividends with workers.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: restore Sure Start (Sure Start Plus); 30 hours free preschool for all 2–4‑year‑olds; more funding for schools; abolish SATs; free school meals for all primary pupils.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; lifelong learning entitlements; fix apprenticeships; Climate Apprenticeships.

Housing
- Build 1m+ social homes over a decade (at least 150k/yr; 100k council); end Right to Buy; real affordability linked to incomes; rent controls and open‑ended tenancies; end “no‑fault” evictions; nationwide landlord licensing; stronger tenants’ rights; tackle homelessness and rough sleeping within five years.

Policing and justice
- Rebuild neighbourhood policing (more officers/PCSOs/staff); victims’ rights standards; restore legal aid; reunify probation; presumption against short prison sentences; invest in youth services and prevention.

Social security and migration
- Scrap Universal Credit; end sanctions, five‑week wait, two‑child limit and benefit cap; uprate Local Housing Allowance; redesign a dignified system.
- End the “hostile environment,” indefinite detention, and close Yarl’s Wood/Brook House; fair compensation for Windrush; protect family reunion; humane asylum with safe routes and right to work.

Democracy and Brexit
- Abolish House of Lords for an elected Senate via constitutional convention; votes at 16; automatic voter registration; stronger transparency and lobbying rules.
- Final‑say referendum within six months: renegotiated deal (customs union, close Single Market alignment, rights and standards) vs Remain; implement the result.

International and defence
- Human-rights‑led foreign policy; War Powers Act; suspend arms sales linked to abuses (e.g., Yemen); recognise Palestine; climate diplomacy restored; 0.7% aid with focus on inequality and climate justice.
- Maintain NATO, spend at least 2% of GDP on defence, renew Trident; improve forces’ pay, housing and veterans’ support.

Digital, culture, media, sport
- Free full‑fibre broadband by 2030 via public British Broadband; Charter of Digital Rights.
- Arts Premium in schools; £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; protect public broadcasters; strengthen media plurality and standards; fair sport governance and grassroots investment.
